qAndA.question: What specific technology does Neal Stephenson believe is not essential for building the metaverse?

qAndA.answer: He highlights the historical context, mentioning that "Doom" came out the year after his book "Snow Crash." He uses this to emphasize how rapidly our perception of the digital world changes with technology.
qAndA.question: How does Neal Stephenson use the video game "Doom" to illustrate his point about technological evolution?

qAndA.answer: He raises his index finger, as if pointing to an idea, each time he mentions his past views and how they have changed.
qAndA.question: What hand gesture does Neal Stephenson repeatedly make while discussing his past assumptions about the metaverse?

qAndA.answer: He often closes his eyes briefly while referencing his past views, conveying a sense of introspection and recalling.
qAndA.question: What specific visual element suggests that Neal Stephenson is reflecting on his past beliefs?

qAndA.answer: Thought-provoking and reflective. He doesn't present definitive answers but rather encourages a reevaluation of common assumptions about the metaverse.

narrativeProgression.description: Stephenson expresses his belief that AR and VR aren't essential for building the metaverse.
He reflects on his past view, formed 30 years ago while writing his book, suggesting an evolution in his perspective.
He reveals his past assumption that the metaverse would be centered around goggles.
Acknowledges a significant shift in understanding and collective learning since then.
Uses the release of the game 'Doom' as a temporal landmark, placing it after his book 'Snow Crash.'
Highlights the difficulty of recalling a time before games like 'Doom,' implying their pervasiveness.
Defines such games as those offering a flat window view into a 3D world, contrasting with immersive experiences.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: We absolutely do not need AR and VR in order to build the Metaverse.
And I, 30 years ago when I wrote the book, I had a different view of it.
And so I assumed that it would be all about goggles.
But a lot has changed since then, and we've all learned a lot.
So Doom came out the year after Snowcrash was published.
And it's kind of almost hard to remember a time when there weren't games like Doom.
Meaning games where your screen is a flat window into a three-dimensional world.

youtube_description:
When author and futurist Neal Stephenson invented the metaverse in his book Snow Crash, it was accessed through VR goggles. But after Doom was released the next year, his thinking about how to view virtual 3D worlds has changed.

Watch his entire a16z Podcast episode here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=60u9L5-YO9Q
youtube_title: We don't need AR and VR to build the metaverse
